survey: A carved jack-o'-lantern on a wooden plank table, seen in three-quarter view from slightly above, face toward the camera. Body: a squat, wide pumpkin with even vertical ribs that meet at a small dip at the top. Stem: a short green stalk that grows out of that top dip and bends slightly to the right. It is joined cleanly and does not float. Face: two triangular eyes and a wide zig-zag mouth are cut into the front of the shell. Each cut shows a beveled inner wall, so it reads as cut through the rind, and the warm yellow glow inside suggests a light within. Simplification: the inside of each cut is a flat glowing plane rather than a view of the hollow interior, which is normal for this kind of card. Support: the round bottom rests on the planks with a soft contact shadow, so the pumpkin is grounded. It has no invented parts and no loose, extra or missing pieces.

errors.what: The two eyes do not match. The left eye is a narrow triangle leaning left with its tip pointing up-left. The right eye is a wider, upright triangle with a level base. On an otherwise symmetric carved face this looks like a mistake rather than a deliberate choice. It is noticeable only on a close look.

fix: Carve two matching mirrored triangular eyes, the same size and tilt, set evenly on either side of the center rib above the zig-zag mouth.
